features.title: Unmanaged AMD64 PE32+ input contract

evidence.claim: Architecture and managed-image rejection are fail-closed.

features.title: Transactional output publication and keyed validation

evidence.claim: Invalid or failed staging never replaces the existing output.
The staged container is authenticated before publication.

features.title: Normal imports and IAT reconstruction

evidence.claim: Native fixtures call imported Windows and CRT functions.
Import inventory is bounded and structurally validated.

features.title: DIR64 relocations at a non-preferred ASLR base

evidence.claim: The packed fixture reports reloc=1 and aslr=1 at runtime.
Relocation parser and native loader contracts are fail-closed.

features.title: Win32 resource lookup after anti-dump hardening

evidence.claim: FindResourceW, LoadResource, and LockResource are checked from protected code.
A DLL whose resource root begins 0x40 bytes inside its owner section preserves the exact DataDirectory pair and byte-matches FindResourceW/LoadResource runtime output.
Analyzer-to-assembler resource owner storage stays distinct from the exact resource directory RVA and size.

features.title: EXE static TLS data and callback lifecycle

evidence.claim: The packed EXE proves main-thread and post-start worker TLS callback/data isolation.
TLS lifecycle source contracts are inspected.

features.title: DLL static TLS data and callback lifecycle

evidence.claim: Loading-thread, post-load worker, pre-existing worker, callback, and 64-byte alignment behavior are compared with the original DLL.
TLS lifecycle source contracts are inspected.

features.title: EXE x64 exception and unwind registration

evidence.claim: A packed C++ throw/catch returns caught=-1 with exact exit parity.
Runtime function-table registration contracts are inspected.

features.title: DLL x64 exception and unwind registration

evidence.claim: A guarded DLL export throws and catches through x64 unwind metadata across eight load/call/unload cycles.

features.title: Delay-load import resolution

evidence.claim: A real /DELAYLOAD dependency call is checked after process startup.
A modern GuardCF delay-load input is packed and byte-compared at runtime.

features.title: DLL delay-load import resolution

evidence.claim: Only bounded RVA-based delay descriptors are accepted and the outer PE preserves the helper-visible directory pair.
The dependency is absent before the first delayed call, present afterward, explicitly unloaded, and remains clean over eight DLL reload cycles.

features.title: Load-config, CFG, XFG, CastGuard, and volatile metadata
features.blocker: GuardCF, exact suppressed/export-suppressed GFIDs, one real EXE XFG signature, and seven real DLL GPR-class ABI shapes pass natively with XFG call-site type hashes preserved byte-exact through materialization; floating-point, vector, aggregate ABI signatures and clean-VM compatibility evidence remain incomplete.

evidence.claim: The preservation plan retains source GFID identities, omits direct-only virtualization thunks, and rejects forged generated thunk targets.
Current MSVC fixtures carry modern GuardCF/XFG load-config variants.

Real MSVC /guard:cf /guard:xfg indirect calls retain the source GFID for one EXE signature and seven DLL GPR-class ABI shapes with arities 0, 1, 2, 3, and 6, including fifth/sixth stack arguments, pointer loads/stores, and a void return; each distinct caller XFG type hash is structurally paired with the XFG dispatch call and remains byte-exact through materialization, direct-only virtualized thunks retain native parity without thunk GFIDs, and forged generated-GFID paths are rejected before output.

features.title: Selected-function virtualization with authenticated paging
features.blocker: Only an explicit scalar function subset is liftable; bounded 32/64-bit SHLD/SHRD are covered, while DIV/IDIV fault delivery, native calls, SIMD/FP, exception-bearing bodies, and indirect/address-taken closure remain unsupported.

evidence.claim: Five selected first-party functions, including one-operand MUL/IMUL with RDX:RAX results, execute identically after virtualization.
Authenticated bytecode page construction and tamper rejection are covered.
Bounded 32/64-bit SHLD/SHRD register and memory destinations, immediate and CL counts, zero-count behavior, writeback, and defined flags match the differential oracle.

features.title: Anti-dump metadata sanitization and protection transitions

evidence.claim: Native fault injection proves header and metadata protection transitions restore protections and fail closed.
Source contracts require checked header erasure, metadata sanitization, protection restoration, and ordering before protected TLS callbacks.
Packed EXE and DLL fixtures execute after anti-dump sanitization while loader-visible resources, exports, and mitigation metadata remain usable.

features.title: Process mitigation and DLL search policy
features.blocker: Pre-import ordering, current-directory DLL planting rejection, and process-policy API fail-closed injections are candidate-bound, but clean-VM representative-application compatibility is not recorded.

evidence.claim: An unhardened packed EXE loads a probe DLL from its launch directory while process hardening rejects it before the protected import or entrypoint executes; deterministic process-mitigation and DLL-search-policy API failures also stop before the entrypoint.
The process policy runs before the first protected LoadLibrary import resolution and remains rejected for DLL payloads.
Candidate staging runs the opt-in native hardening file with the exact freshly built stub path and records artifact-bound evidence.

features.title: Anti-debug detection and host-safe failure
features.blocker: Positive DEBUG_PROCESS behavior is proven locally for an EXE and for host-safe protected-DLL rejection, but clean-VM debugger/tool and representative-host compatibility evidence are missing.

evidence.claim: A DEBUG_PROCESS control reaches the protected EXE entrypoint while its anti-debug variant exits before the marker; a debugged host rejects an anti-debug protected DLL without terminating the host.
DLL anti-debug paths return failure to the host without ExitProcess and use reliable debug-port checks.
Candidate staging binds the positive DEBUG_PROCESS EXE proof to the exact freshly built stub hash.

features.title: Native executable-page memory guard
features.blocker: Forced-ASLR DIR64 relocation, 24-thread concurrent first-touch, and a bounded one-minute minimum-64-launch process soak are candidate-bound, but multi-hour and clean-VM coverage remain missing.

evidence.claim: The opt-in native matrix forces a non-preferred base, exercises an executable DIR64 pointer, synchronizes 24 threads on first access to one protected page, and repeats at least 64 protected launches for at least one minute.
Known memory-guard fault, tamper, recursion, and protection-transition paths have regression checks.
Candidate staging runs the native memory-guard matrix with the exact freshly built stub and hashes its evidence record into the manifest.

features.title: DLL loader-lock dependency initialization

evidence.claim: All protected imports are represented in the outer import table and captured before DllMain; native hosts cover success, no-entry, and rejected attach cleanup.

features.title: Dynamic-load exports and unload/reload lifecycle

evidence.claim: One dynamic host resolves and calls the test exports.

features.title: Static-import consumers of packed DLL exports

evidence.claim: A native static-import host resolves the authenticated plaintext export snapshot before StubDllMain.

The tracked prebuilt records legacy-unverified provenance.

features.title: Clean-VM Windows compatibility, signing, and scanner evidence
features.blocker: No recorded clean-VM matrix proves current Windows versions, Authenticode signing/timestamping, Defender scanning, and real application workflows.
